cobbleandcandle.title: Cobble & Candle
cobbleandcandle.blurb: A WordPress block theme for restaurants, taverns and inns: menus with diet filters, live “open now” hours, table and room bookings, events, and a setup wizard. No page builder.
cobbleandcandle.eyebrow: Theme in progress · Restaurants, taverns & inns
cobbleandcandle.summary: Cobble & Candle is a WordPress block theme for restaurants, taverns and inns. Guests see live “open now” hours, menus they can filter by diet, and book a table or a room. Owners set it up in a five-step wizard, import a menu from a spreadsheet, and confirm bookings from the dashboard. It is not in the shop yet.
cobbleandcandle.challenge: Hospitality sites go stale fast. Hours change on holidays, menus change weekly, and most restaurant themes are page-builder demos with static text. An inn with a restaurant downstairs usually needs a second booking plugin and a calendar sync service on top.
cobbleandcandle.approach: I built it as a block theme on Sage 11 with a companion plugin that owns the data: locations, hours, menus, events, rooms and bookings. “Open now” is worked out in the visitor’s browser so cached pages stay right. Rooms get a real availability calendar with two-way iCal sync. Everything is edited in WordPress itself: the Site Editor for design, short field panels for prices and hours.
cobbleandcandle.result: A restaurant, bar or inn gets a site that tells guests whether it is open, what is on the menu, and lets them request a table or a room in under a minute. The live demo is at cobbleandcandle.matthummel.com with fiction content. It is not for sale yet; say hello if you want it for your place or want me to set it up.
cobbleandcandle.audience: Restaurant, tavern and inn owners who want menus, hours and bookings that stay right without a developer. Agencies that ship hospitality sites. Hiring managers who want to see a full WordPress product: theme, plugin, booking engine, setup wizard, docs and tests.
cobbleandcandle.architecture: Sage 11 block theme (Acorn, Blade, Tailwind v4, Vite, Alpine.js) with 28 server-rendered blocks and four Site Editor style variations (Lampwright, Ember & Arch, Ashlar & Iron, Daylight). Cobble & Candle Core plugin (bundled, one-click install) holds locations, menus, events, rooms, bookings and messages as custom post types with REST-registered fields. Booking engine: availability endpoint, pending → confirmed requests, hourly iCal import and a private export feed per room. Restaurant, Menu, Event, HotelRoom, Organization, WebSite and BreadcrumbList schema, joined to Yoast or Rank Math when present. WCAG 2.2 AA, right-to-left languages, translation-ready.
cobbleandcandle.handoff: Upload the theme, click once to install the plugin, and the setup wizard asks for your name, style, currency and clock, imports the demo or your first location, and builds the pages and menus. Hours and holiday hours are set per location; menus import from a CSV. A Status page checks the setup and gives a system report for support.

faq: Is Cobble & Candle a WordPress restaurant theme?
Yes. It is a WordPress block theme for restaurants, taverns and inns, with menus, live opening hours, table bookings, events, private dining and rooms to stay, built without a page builder.
Can I buy Cobble & Candle?
Not yet. It is finished and running on the live demo, and I am getting it ready for the shop. Say hello if you want it for your restaurant, bar or inn sooner, or want me to set it up.
Does it handle rooms for a B&B or inn?

Yes. Rooms have nightly and weekend prices, a minimum stay and an availability calendar. Guests send a booking request, you confirm it from the dashboard, and the guest gets an email. Calendars sync both ways with Airbnb, Booking.com and Vrbo.
Does it take payments?
No, on purpose. Table and room bookings are requests you confirm, so there is no card handling or refund process to manage. Link your online-ordering system for takeaway.
Will my hours be right for Google?
Each location publishes Restaurant structured data with opening and holiday hours, address, map coordinates, cuisine and price range. It works alongside Yoast SEO or Rank Math.
Can I import my menu?
Yes. Food & drink → Import / export takes a CSV from Excel or Google Sheets, shows a preview of what will be added or updated, and never deletes anything.
Is it accessible?
It is built and tested for WCAG 2.2 AA: keyboard paths, screen-reader labels, contrast in all four styles, 44 px touch targets and reduced motion. It also supports right-to-left languages.
What do I need to run it?
WordPress 6.6 or newer and PHP 8.3 or newer. Caching plugins such as LiteSpeed Cache and WP Rocket are supported.

faq: Is Acreline a real estate theme?
Yes. Acreline is a WordPress real estate theme for offices that need listings, a map, agents, and showing requests — without a suburban MLS skin or Elementor stack.
Does Acreline include a setup wizard?
Yes. After you activate the theme, Appearance → Acreline Setup walks identity, color style, and optional demo content. You can skip it and use Customize anytime.
What do I get when I buy Acreline?

The marketplace pack: acreline.zip (upload in Appearance → Themes), optional child theme, Acreline Core plugin, and HTML documentation. Instant download after checkout. The theme includes the setup wizard. Hire me if you want branded installation or inventory import.
Is Acreline a live MLS or IDX theme?

No. It ships with demo inventory you manage in WordPress. Listings are a custom post type agencies edit in wp-admin. Wire a real MLS/IDX feed later — the UI does not depend on IDX chrome and the post type survives a theme switch via Acreline Core.
How does a real estate agency edit page copy?

Marketing pages use Core Gutenberg blocks with live ServerSideRender previews — your agents edit them directly in wp-admin. Listings, agents, and bookings use classic metaboxes. Brand, phone, and colors stay in Customize → Identity (or the setup wizard). No developer needed for day-to-day edits.
Can I white-label Acreline for a client real estate agency?

Yes. Theme code is GPLv2 or later. Sage / Acorn remain MIT (GPL-compatible). You can install it for a client agency, customize it, resell services on top, or fork it as a white-label base. The child theme is included for safe agency customization.
Do I need Elementor or ACF for Acreline?

No. Marketing pages use the included Gutenberg blocks. Listings and agents use metaboxes. Identity lives in the Customizer and the setup wizard. Do not install a page builder — it adds no value and conflicts with the block architecture.
Can you install or customize Acreline for my real estate office?

Yes. Buy the pack for self-serve, or Get help and I brand it, import your listings, and hand off wp-admin editing to your brokers. I can also wire a real MLS feed or build custom listing filters for your market.

tocguide.title: TOCguide
tocguide.blurb: A free WordPress plugin that builds a table of contents from post headings — plus an optional Reading Guide.
tocguide.summary: TOCguide is a WordPress plugin that builds a table of contents from the headings in a post. The outline is in the first HTML. An optional Reading Guide adds section previews, read time, and study tools — no accounts, no tracking.
tocguide.challenge: Long posts need a jump list. Many plugins add extra blocks or hide the outline from search engines and screen readers.
tocguide.approach: I built a light plugin that reads headings and prints the list on the first page load. Reading Guide, citations, and study tools stay opt-in. Nothing phones home.
tocguide.result: A publisher can add a table of contents that is easy to read and easy to find. The plugin is free. Hire me if you want it tailored.
tocguide.audience: Writers, shops, and agencies that publish long posts. Also hiring managers who want to see a small plugin I shipped.
tocguide.architecture: PHP block render callback (`tocguide/table-of-contents`), small editor script, optional ItemList JSON-LD. Reading Guide and study tools compute from post content or localStorage. No React runtime on the front end for the list itself. Independent slug: tocguide.
tocguide.handoff: Download the zip, turn the plugin on, and add the block. Settings are under Settings → TOCguide. Source is on GitHub if you want to fork it.

faq: Is TOCguide really free?
Yes. $0 checkout captures your email for update notices if you want them, or download from GitHub Releases. No freemium lock.
Is TOCguide the same plugin as TOCflow?
Yes. TOCguide is the current name and slug (WordPress.org guideline 17). Re-insert the block and save Settings → TOCguide if you used an earlier zip.
Does it work with classic editor posts?
Yes — use the [tocguide] shortcode. Heading anchors still inject on the front end.
Will it slow my site?
The list is in the first HTML response. Front-end JS is optional for sticky, scroll-spy, and study tools, and it respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Does it track readers?
No. No accounts, no analytics, no remote APIs. Study tools that use localStorage stay on the visitor's device.
Can you customize it for my theme?
Yes. Get help for sticky-header offsets, style presets that match your brand, or a private fork.
